by.claim: The freshness signal that would detect syncing stale hydrated files already exists and is simply unconsumed: the hydrator writes a hydrator.metadata file carrying drySHA, commitTime and the reproduction commands alongside each manifest.yaml, and the proposed fix for the push-to-stage staleness bug is precisely an app annotation timestamp compared against that hydrator.metadata. Today nothing compares them, so an auto-sync that deploys whatever the stage branch last held before the external promoter moved fresh manifests is unobservable except as the wrong workload running.

The freshness signal that would detect syncing stale hydrated files already exists and is simply unconsumed: the hydrator writes a hydrator.metadata file carrying drySHA, commitTime and the reproduction commands alongside each manifest.yaml, and the proposed fix for the push-to-stage staleness bug is precisely an app annotation timestamp compared against that hydrator.metadata. Today nothing compares them, so an auto-sync that deploys whatever the stage branch last held before the external promoter moved fresh manifests is unobservable except as the wrong workload running.

The RollingSync failure in which the rollout reports complete while child Applications are OutOfSync is unobservable in production: the only signal named is ApplicationSet status.applicationStatus, which is exactly the field that reports Healthy while the child is OutOfSync, and the reporter's controller logs were at warn level so no progressive-sync transition lines were emitted at all. The four measurements requested for progressive sync are time-to-trigger, time-to-complete-step-X, count of Application refreshes caused by the ApplicationSet, and which Application a sync is waiting on — none of them would move when a step is promoted to Healthy without a sync operation being created, so even after the requested metrics land this failure mode still has no number attached to it.
